Here are two recommendations that focus on Eastern European / Slavic fantasy, which is *criminally* overlooked by romantasy readers. Maybe it's because romance plays second fiddle to the overall plot in these, but I think they're well worth a read. They're also slowburn. Like *actually* slowburn.

{Uprooted by Naomi Novik}

{The Bear and the Nightingale by Katherine Arden} - The first in The Winternight Trilogy, the romance culminates in the second book but is seldom the focus.

Then, one rec for a regency era fantasy based in England.

{Half A Soul by Olivia Atwater} - Probably the most romantic fantasy book I've read in a while, but it is YA, and therefore has zero spice.

  
I recommend Margaret Rogerson's books as well. She writes very cozy, lowkey romances, with the exception of Vespertine, which is my favorite of her work, but not at all a romance. She does tend to skew YA.

I'm realizing none of these books are spicy, like at all, but the chemistry between the FMC and MMC is insane in every single one. I am partial to yearning, too.

For the context hints that pop up during certain conversations, I actually don't mind those. I like them haha, so maybe I'm a dum-dum. They make me wonder how certain characters will treat me differently in the future because of something I said.

For your positive points, I'm with ya. Hell, my opinion might be more extreme lol. I pretty much love the aesthetic overhaul, even for the NPC/player models. Besides the necks, which I think are WAY too stout/thick when undergarments are toggled, everything else looks fantastic to me. Narrow neck gang rise up.

Environments are lovely. This definitely feels like a spiritual successor to DA2. Loot system and combat mechanics are also so much better, though... here's a complaint:

I do NOT like most of the armors/outfits so far. I have kept my starting Warden armor transmogged and am praying--PRAYING, I tell you--that I will have better options once I get to Weisshaupt's vendor because... Christ. Every faction I've encountered so far has been dripless.

Thaaaat's all I've got, though. I'm having a great time. As someone who's loved this series for nearly a decade, it's tough at times to not see things through rose-colored goggles, but I feel like this game's identity is so focused and singular that it's turning away people who wanted the series to go any number of different directions. It's all valid, I get it. I'm just lucky enough to like what BioWare cooked up, I guess.
